text:
maya: Heads up — after the token-bucket change to continuous batching we started seeing weird streaming interactions on prod. p95 token latency up ~35% for small streams. Looks like flush cadence is creating a lot of tiny partial-decodes that kill kernel utilization.

jonathan: Can you paste a simple repro or a trace? Is this only with streaming enabled or all generation?

maya: Only observed with streaming. Non-streaming batches still look fine. Attached a short profiler snippet from last canary:
```
[trace] batch_size=1..8 median_tokens=12 target_token_budget=64
kernel_util=0.27 (was 0.78 pre-change)
partial_decodes=high
flush_events_per_sec=4200
mean_batch_latency=14ms (node), p95=220ms
```

rik: Hmm. That flush_events_per_sec number is huge. Token-bucket target 64 with the new immediate-flush-on-first-output policy will often force an early flush when the first token is emitted, especially for interactive prompts. Result: lots of <4 token micro-batches.

sam: That matches the oncall noise. Users saw more jitter during chats with the canary. Are there queued requests that get starved by repeated early flushes?

maya: Yes — queue depth shows churn. The continuous sampler currently prioritizes latency and will flush when per-request latency_budget is hit, ignoring global token_budget. So streaming responses win local latency but destroy throughput.

karen: Posted a quick A/B from staging:
```
A: old policy (flush_on_output=false) -> avg_gpu_util=0.82, p95_streaming=180ms
B: new policy (flush_on_output=true) -> avg_gpu_util=0.29, p95_streaming=240ms, cost_per_1000_tokens +22%
```

jonathan: I think we need a hybrid queue policy: prefer accumulating until either global token_budget or time_budget (e.g., 15ms) but allow an override for high-priority <latency> routes. Also consider marking streaming-first-output as a soft hint, not mandatory flush.

rik: Agreed. Two knobs to try: (1) make per-request flush threshold proportional to remaining budget so long-running requests don't preempt tiny ones, (2) add a "streaming_min_batch_tokens" floor so we don't flush if queued batch tokens < X unless time_budget exceeded.

maya: Proposed config snippet for experiments:
```json
{"continuous": {
  "global_token_budget": 128,
  "per_request_flush_pct": 0.25,
  "streaming_min_batch_tokens": 24,
  "max_flush_latency_ms": 20,
  "prefer_latency_routes": ["/chat/stream","/tool/call"],
  "queue_policy": "age_and_size_priority"
}}
```

perf-bot: Automated run results (staging canary 1769005400 -> 1769005500): avg_gpu_util +0.41, p95_streaming down 12ms when streaming_min_batch_tokens=24, cost delta -6%.

sam: Nice. Any regression risk for really low-latency apps (e.g., 1 token responses)?

rik: We should add an escape hatch: if a single request has explicit header `x-force-stream-flush: 1` then do immediate flush. Otherwise use hybrid policy. Also we can detect single-token completions and short-circuit decode path to avoid building full batch when it's wasteful.

jonathan: We'll need unit tests around partial-decode scheduling and a perf harness: create synthetic workload with 60% streams short(<=8 tokens), 40% batch long(>64 tokens) and sweep streaming_min_batch_tokens [8,16,24,48].

maya: I'll run the sweep on staging tonight and post numbers. Plan: revert canary if cost delta > +10% or p95 for streaming rises.

karen: One more blip we saw — KV cache hits actually increase sensitivity: when a request reuses KV cache and returns output faster, the first-output flush triggers earlier. So the policy must consider estimated remaining decode tokens after KV reuse. Maybe use model-estimated remaining_tokens to adapt flush decisions.

maya: Good call. I'll add `estimated_remaining_tokens` into the batch scorer and try biasing against flushing if remaining_tokens < threshold.

deploy-bot: Canary rolled back at 1769005600 to previous kernel selection patch (automatic safety rollback trigger).

maya: Repro steps I used:
1) start local perf harness with 100 qps, 60% streaming short prompts
2) enable continuous batching token-bucket with target=64 and flush_on_first_output=true
3) measure gpu_util and partial_decode_count

jonathan: Thanks — please also capture per-kernel launch count. If partial-decodes multiply kernel launches we might be hitting kernel launch overheads on some GPUs.

maya: Yep adding that. Will post new trace + config results in morning. :coffee:
